account:
Today town business has been mostly quiet, but there is uncertainty around grain deliveries and the miller’s whereabouts. I went to the mill for the scheduled ten o’clock grain inspection and could not locate the miller, leaving the stocks unverified. Both the baker and neighbour also say they have been unable to find or see the miller today. That is unusual, but I do not know why the miller is absent.

Several townsfolk have repeated vague reports about bridge or port changes affecting the bakery. I have seen no such change myself. The baker says they have no confirmed news of shortages or access changes, and the secretary has received no confirmed changes either. The baker reported that freight delivered wheat last night and that the bread stall is well stocked. These reports give no firm basis for declaring a supply problem.

The neighbour previously reported seeing the baker give bread to the innkeeper yesterday, hearing the innkeeper ask about spare wheat or hay, and hearing that freight sought the miller about arrangements. This may simply be ordinary provisioning and delivery coordination; I cannot establish any other purpose from what I know.

No new council correspondence arrived this afternoon. I am now at the neighbour’s cottage for our three o’clock tea, and they have invited me inside and asked about my morning. My remaining appointments are the office at 16:30 and the confirmed lighting inspection with the builder inside the great hall at 18:00, followed by home at 19:00.
